title: Deep-learning ultrasound AI identifies benign thyroid nodules to spare aspirations
summary: A deep-learning ultrasound system re-evaluated 4,572 nodules that radiologists judged suspicious and that underwent FNA; it correctly identified 2,719 of 3,134 benign nodules (86.8%), which would reduce FNA from 68.5% to 9.1%, while missing 123 malignant nodules (8.6%). In a comparison cohort it identified 81.4% (96/118) as benign versus 40% and 55% for radiologists, AUC 0.88. The study is retrospective, 8.6% of malignant nodules were missed and independence from the training data is not stated.
ai_technology: Pre-existing deep-learning ultrasound AI system re-evaluating thyroid nodules to identify benign nodules
organization: Shanghai Tenth People's Hospital, Tongji University

evidence.tested: Retrospective multicenter validation cohort of 4,572 nodules with cytology or pathology outcomes, plus a separate radiologist comparison cohort.
evidence.unknown: Prospective effect on FNA decisions; independence of the validation cohorts from model training; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning ultrasound system classified nodules as benign to select patients who could avoid FNA.
